Dranx Prediction League · UI/UX audit

Faster answers, clearer scoring and fewer taps: a redesign proposal for every public workflow

This audit covers the production site after the September 2026 redesign. The season is revealed, matchweek 6 of Win Streak is open, and 14 entries are live. Each section shows a live "before" capture and an HTML render of the proposed redesign. All renders use real public data and the existing Dranx tokens: warm paper, purple identity, lime actions and the original club badges.

22 Sep 2026 Production · read-only 390 · 320 · 1280 px Light + dark 17 findings · 9 redesign renders
Summary 1 · Shell & nav 2 · Season table 3 · Leaderboard 4 · Entry detail 5 · Spotlight 6 · Win Streak 7 · Rules 8 · Next-season entry 9 · Colour & dark 10 · Owner desk Roadmap

Summary

The redesign's foundations are strong. It has zero axe violations, 56px handles, honest tie handling, safe-area actions and no horizontal overflow. The remaining problems are about information density and semantic signalling. On a phone, most pages spend the first screen on headings and metadata before showing the answer the visitor came for. Several colour choices also give the wrong message: scores look like errors and small gains look like warnings.

Constraints every render respects

  • The points podium stays and is grouped by occupied competition ranks 1–3, so every tied participant receives equal styling. Animal icons still derive from display names.
  • Table points (capped at 100) and Spotlight accuracy stay visually and semantically separate.
  • No new personal data, no runtime football feed, and no unrevealed picks. Win Streak current picks remain public by design.
  • Tap targets stay at 44px or more, sorting handles at 56px, and names, ranks and numbers carry meaning without colour.

1App shell, navigation and page intros

Every public page opens with a two-row header (brand row plus five text links), then an H1, a subtitle, a status badge and up to three meta lines. At 390px the Season table shows its first club about 450px down. At 320px the nav links touch each other and the club names break mid-word.

F5 · Intros spend the first screen on metadata

The line "Updated 20 Sep 2026, 13:13 CDT · 20 Sep 2026, 18:13 UTC" appears on Season table, Leaderboard and Entry, often on two lines. A friends' league needs one local time; UTC can live in a title or a details disclosure. Merge "2026/27 Premier League · Submissions closed · predictions revealed" into one meta row.

src/components/page-heading.tsx · src/features/standings/season-table-page.tsx · src/app/leaderboard/page.tsx
F6 · Top nav is crowded and out of thumb reach

At 320px the five links sit about 4px apart and the header uses about 120px. On phones, a fixed bottom tab bar with icon and label frees about 70px of header and puts navigation within thumb reach. Desktop keeps the current underline nav.

src/components/site-header.tsx · src/components/site-navigation.tsx
F4 · Mid-word breaks at 320px

[overflow-wrap:anywhere] on club and participant names produces "Mancheste / r City". Use overflow-wrap:break-word with hyphens:auto, and let the badge column shrink first. anywhere also lowers the min-content width, which is why the grid picks the broken layout.

season-table-page.tsx:84, :267 · entries/[id]/page.tsx:133 · leaderboard-board.tsx:64, :247 · spotlight-views.tsx:132
  • Single-row app bar naming the current page, plus a bottom tab bar below 640px. This gives back about 70px, and the tabs are 64×48px targets.
  • One meta line in local time. "Provisional ⓘ" explains itself on tap (F14).
  • Zone legend sits directly above the table, so the rail colours finally mean something (F14).
  • The first club appears at about 190px instead of about 450px, and 11 clubs fit on one screen instead of 5.

2Season table: make the gap readable

F3 · Gap colour bands don't encode direction

Today the chips use a "near / slight / far" band per sign, but the near bands are yellow (+) and orange (−), so +0.8 Nottingham Forest and +0.2 Sunderland look like warnings. Readers also have to parse ▲/▼ to learn direction. Use a diverging scale: greens for above expectation, rose to crimson for below, and neutral grey within ±1 place. Keep the arrows and numbers so colour stays redundant.

src/features/standings/season-table-page.tsx:30–40 (band logic) · globals.css gap tokens
  • On desktop, add a small "Your prediction" column when the browser holds a prediction receipt. Keep it local-only and never serialized publicly.
  • Move "How to read the gap" into a ⓘ popover on the Gap header so the aside can hold both surprise cards above the fold.

3Leaderboard: the answer first

The leaderboard is the most-visited question ("where am I?"), and on mobile it takes the most scrolling. The heading, meta, "Find a participant" form and podium come first. The full list then starts again at rank 1, so the top three appear twice. Each list row is about 80px tall because it stacks a name, a repeated "Arsenal" champion line, a "TABLE POINTS" label and a thin /100 bar.

F1 · Ranking below the first screen, duplicated podium, tall rows

Keep the podium, since the brand requires it, but make it a compact three-step strip. Start the list at the first rank not on the podium. Rows become about 52px with a score-breakdown bar (exact / within 3 / half) that turns the chips hidden on mobile into a glanceable visual. Show the champion pick only as a badge (the Arsenal crest) rather than a text line repeated 12 times. Replace the "Find" submit form with instant filtering, since there are 14 names.

src/features/leaderboard/leaderboard-board.tsx · podium.tsx · movement.ts · src/app/leaderboard/page.tsx
F2 · Scores look like errors

Table points render in magenta-red (the same family as the danger colour), so a 40-point leader looks penalised. Use brand ink for scores and keep red for regressions only (▼ movement).

F14 · Movement arrows lack a reference

"▲1" under the rank doesn't say "since the 13 Sep table". Add a caption on the header ("Movement since last table: 13 Sep") and an aria-label per row.

  • The first screen now answers "who's winning, and by how much?" for 10 of 14 people, where before it showed only the first podium card.
  • The breakdown bar is dark green for exact, mid-green for within 3 and lilac for half. It's a proportional 5/3/1-point stack, and a screen reader hears "3 exact, 7 within three, 4 half; 40 points".
  • With a prediction receipt in this browser, a lime "You · 5th · 30 pts" bar pins above the list and scrolls to the row. Without one, nothing changes.
  • Ties keep shared rank numbers (5, 5 · 9, 9, 9), and the podium stays grouped by occupied rank. When several people tie for 1st, the 1st step lists all of them.

4Entry detail: tell the story of one prediction

F7 · 20 identical tall rows, no summary, no way to compare

Each row repeats "ACTUAL" and "DIFFERENCE" labels. The 40/100 score sits in the meta row, and nothing tells you how it was earned until you read all 20 rows. The 1-point pill is danger pink (F2). You also can't move to the next entry without going back.

src/app/entries/[id]/page.tsx
  • Score hero plus a breakdown bar explains 40 = 3×5 + 7×3 + 4×1 at a glance, and the filter chips jump straight to the misses.
  • Labels move to one column header, taking rows from about 56px to 44px. "Off" shows the absolute difference, and the points pill uses the 5/3/1/0 scale (green → lilac → grey) instead of danger pink.
  • "1st of 14 ›" steps through entries in leaderboard order. "Compare with…" overlays another revealed entry's predicted position per club (a public projection after reveal only).
  • Per-club scoring still leads, and Spotlight follows, as AGENTS.md requires.

5Spotlight: one tap per category, a matrix that fits

F8 · Select plus "Show category" is a two-action selector

The native <select> and submit button are good for progressive enhancement, but with JS the selector should apply instantly. The seven categories fit in a horizontally scrollable chip row with role="tablist", and the select can stay as the no-JS fallback. "Current leader" repeats row 1, so fold it into the first row as a "Leader" tag. "Select to see names" should be the tap affordance itself: a stacked-avatar button that expands inline.

src/features/leaderboard/spotlight-views.tsx · src/app/spotlight/page.tsx
F9 · Matrix shows 1.3 of 7 columns on mobile

Below 640px, transpose it: one compact card per entry with seven mini result cells in a 4+3 grid, or keep the grid with a sticky name column, a right-edge fade and a "7 categories →" hint.

  • The chip row keeps "all seven boards through a selector" (AGENTS.md) while removing the submit round trip. Keep the ?category= URL so views stay shareable and back-button safe.
  • The matrix card total is illustrative. Derive it from the existing accuracy model and never persist it.

6Win Streak: a weekly habit loop

Win Streak is the only part of the product people return to every week, but the page is built like a one-time form. Returning players with a receipt get their panel, yet the deadline is plain text, fixture kickoff times are hidden below 1024px (hidden … lg:block), and used clubs appear only as disabled buttons with no reason. On the public board, each row's "No pick yet" sits on its own divided line and reads as a separate empty row.

F10 · The board's row structure and hidden kickoffs

Put the pick inline on the same row (badge and club, or "– not picked"). Show kickoff times on every width, grouped under day headers ("Sat 3 Oct"), because the time is the difference between a safe and a risky pick.

src/features/win-streak/win-streak-leaderboard.tsx · win-streak-entry-panel.tsx:556–612
F11 · No urgency and no reasoning

Add a countdown to the round lock and a "Won in MW3" caption on unavailable clubs. Returning players (receipt present) should see their streak card and the pick grid first, and new visitors should see the board first with "Join" as a secondary card. The streak mechanic (wins restrict clubs; draws and losses reset and unlock) should appear as a three-icon strip, not a paragraph.

7Rules: player-facing, not operator-facing

F12 · A 3,983px page with implementation detail mixed in

Participants meet max(0, N + 1 − occupied outcome rank), "578 supplied portraits appear locally", "internally reconciled roster", "canonical season player", "reviewed dataset" and a "Current data status" box describing when things publish. Split it into three tabs (Table · Spotlight · Win Streak), each opening with a worked example. Move data-operations notes to the owner docs (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). The interactive "Try a scoring example" works well; extend the same pattern to Spotlight and Win Streak.

src/app/rules/page.tsx · src/components/how-to-play.tsx · scoring-example.tsx

8Next-season entry: get to the table faster

Submissions are closed for 2026/27, so these recommendations target the 2027/28 opening. The owner-approved three-stage flow, the draft and the A–Z acknowledgement stay. Only the order of what's on screen changes.

F13 · Stage 1 shows a single club above the fold

The "Who is making this prediction?" card and the A–Z warning together take about 520px, and the sticky action takes about 100px. Only Arsenal is visible. Ordering 20 clubs by drag alone is also slow: moving Tottenham from 18th to 5th takes a long thumb-drag with auto-scroll.

src/features/predictions/prediction-form.tsx · prediction-sorter.tsx · alphabetical-order-dialog.tsx
  • Name becomes an inline field (it's still the only personal data). The A–Z warning becomes a one-line banner with a live "N of 20 moved" counter, and "Why?" opens the existing explanation.
  • Tap a position number to open a "Move to…" sheet: pick 1–20 or top/bottom. Drag and keyboard (Arrow, Page Up/Down, Home/End) stay as they are, so this is an additional, faster path, not a replacement.
  • Stage 2 (below): replace the "Type at least 2 letters to search 580 players… Up to 20 matches" intro with a 7-dot progress row. Keep the 2-character search rule in the field's own helper text, and collapse completed categories to one-line summaries so the unfinished ones rise.

9Colour semantics and dark mode

F2 (system-wide) · One points scale, used everywhere

Today, table points are magenta, 1-point results are danger pink, 3-point results are sky blue and 5-point results are mint. Define a single scoring scale token set (below) and use it for leaderboard breakdowns, entry pills, spotlight ranks and matrix cells. Reserve danger for errors and negative movement.

Scoring scale (light)
5 · Exact3 · Within 31 · Correct half0 · Missed

The scale steps from strong green to mint, lilac and neutral. It's ordinal, so more points get more ink. Each pill keeps its number and label.

Before · dark mode leaderboard

F15 · The "Find" button's --brand fill (#37003c) on #17131a has a non-text contrast of about 1.3:1, so it reads as a hole. In dark mode, use brand-ink-dark (#e7c7eb) or the lime primary. The "Provisional" badge also shouts; soften it to warning-soft-dark with a lighter ring.

F16 · Footer weight

The two-paragraph disclaimer is bold, uses body size and sits on a tinted band on every page (about 250px on mobile). Keep the text but set it at 12px regular, and link "Club marks & data" to a details page.

src/components/site-footer.tsx

10Owner desk (brief)

F17 · Operator ergonomics

Admin pages carry the public five-link nav, then a six-pill admin nav with a full-width Sign out, then a jargon-dense intro ("publishing moves one exact immutable snapshot into public scoring… against that same active pointer"). The owner can't see which of the five result datasets are published, drafted or stale without opening each. Suggestions: hide the public nav under /admin (keep a "View site" link), add a status board (below), and rewrite intros in task language ("Enter the goals table, check it, then publish"). Keep every safeguard: typed LOCK/REVEAL, attestation and compare-and-swap.

Suggested roadmap

Quick wins · 1–2 days
  • F4 replace overflow-wrap:anywhere on names
  • F2 scores in brand ink, plus the unified 5/3/1/0 scale
  • F3 diverging gap scale with an "as expected" band
  • F5 one meta line, local time only
  • F10 inline Win Streak pick, and kickoff times at all widths
  • F14 Provisional ⓘ, zone legend, movement caption
  • F15 dark primary contrast · F16 footer weight
Medium · about a week
  • F1 compact podium strip and dense leaderboard rows with breakdown bar
  • F7 entry summary, filters and previous/next
  • F8 instant category chips (keep the select as no-JS fallback)
  • F9 mobile matrix transpose
  • F11 countdown, used-club reasons, outcome-stating review sheet
  • F12 Rules split into three tabs, ops notes moved to docs
Before 2027/28 opens
  • F6 mobile bottom tab bar
  • F13 inline name, A–Z counter banner, tap-to-move sheet
  • Stage 2 progress dots and collapsed completed picks
  • "You" pin on leaderboards when a receipt is present
  • F17 owner status board
Each change must still pass the Definition of Done in AGENTS.md: unit and component tests, isolated Neon integration, 320–430px reflow, 56px handles, keyboard/touch/mouse, dark mode, axe, and no public serialization of unrevealed data. The "You" pin must read only the local receipt and must never add a public field.

Method. Read-only Playwright captures of pl-predictions-2026.vercel.app on 22 Sep 2026 at 390×844 (iPhone 13, DPR 3), 320×640, and 1280×800 in light and dark schemes. No production writes, sign-ins, Win Streak profiles or form submissions were made. Stage 1/2 and owner-desk "before" images come from the repository's isolated QA captures (public/how-to-play/, docs/assets/qa/redesign/). Source was reviewed at 577f08b.

Renders. The "after" phones are static HTML/CSS mockups built from DESIGN.md tokens, the owner-provided club badges and the licensed local portraits. Participant names and scores match the public production leaderboard at capture time. Win Streak fixtures, countdowns and admin rows are illustrative.
